The objective is to combine overall player ability with head-to-head statistics to produce an accurate estimate. The method draws inspiration from Stern and Sugano (2006) who use a beta-binomial model, and Bill James' log5 formula. The approach starts with a prior distribution representing baseline expectations when no prior data exists between a batter and pitcher. This process reflects a core principle of Bayesian inference: belief updates through evidence integration. The framework allows for uncertainty quantification and adaptive learning, crucial for predictive modeling in sports analytics. The intercept reflects baseline performance against average opposition, while the slope quantifies responsiveness to changes in opponent strength. The hypothesis that intercepts vary implies heterogeneity in player abilities, which is critical for accurate predictive modeling. The model also raises questions about whether slopes themselves vary, suggesting potential for deeper hierarchical structures.
